note.headline: Mega-cap tech masks a narrow, bear-steepening session with weak breadth
note.standfirst: The S&P and Nasdaq 100 closed higher on AMD, Tesla, and Nvidia, but decliners outnumbered advancers 17 to 8 and the Dow fell. Positioning that leans on index headlines is missing a Treasury curve steepening on falling yields and a dollar that firmed against nearly everything.
takeaways: Index gains came from five names, not a broad advance, with decliners beating advancers more than two to one.
Treasury yields fell across the curve but short rates fell more than long rates, steepening 2s10s by 6bp and 5s30s by 7bp.
The dollar index rose 0.72% even as yields dropped, a combination that does not fit a simple rate-differential story.
VIX fell 9.01% and VVIX fell 9.67%, easing the cost of protection even as breadth and credit stayed weak.
note.desk_view:
The headline tape says risk-on. The internals say something narrower. Nasdaq 100 added 1.35% and the Russell 2000 rose 0.89%, but the advance-decline line closed 8 to 17 and dispersion sat at 2.73. That is a market where a handful of names, AMD up 11.04%, Tesla up 4.23%, Nvidia up 2.78%, carried the tape while staples, materials, real estate, and financials all gave ground. The level that decides which read is correct is breadth: if advancers do not expand behind the next leg higher, this stays a concentration story, not a risk rally.

The bond market is not confirming the equity story either. Yields fell across the curve, 2-year down 12bp to 4.46%, 10-year down 6bp to 4.84%, but the front end fell more than the long end. That is a bear steepener in miniature, and it moved alongside a VIX down 9.01% and a MOVE index down 5.26%, both easing from stressed levels rather than starting from calm. Credit did not join the rally. LQD and HYG both lost ground on the day, and JNK sits at a fresh low for the period. The setup into tomorrow is a market pricing relief in options markets without the same relief showing up in credit spreads or market breadth.
watching: Whether advance-decline breadth turns positive or the rally stays concentrated in five to ten names.
Credit spreads, particularly HYG and JNK, for confirmation or divergence from the equity bid.
The dollar index against EUR/USD and AUD/USD for follow-through on today's 0.72% move.
VIX term structure, given VIX9D fell 16.78% versus VIX3M down 3.72%, for whether the front end stays bid into any event risk.
note.equities:
The S&P 500 closed up 0.32% at 7376.86 and the Nasdaq 100 added 1.35% to 26989.99, while the Dow fell 0.46% and the NYSE Composite was roughly flat. Five names did the work: AMD rose 11.04%, Tesla 4.23%, Nvidia 2.78%, Meta 0.84%, and Oracle 0.82%. Technology and communications were the only sectors with a convincing green print, up 1.45% and 0.43% respectively.

Away from those names the tape was softer. Consumer staples fell 1.28%, materials fell 0.73%, real estate fell 0.68%, and financials fell 0.59%. Breadth confirms the divergence: 17 decliners against 8 advancers in the tracked set, with dispersion at 2.73. Laggards were concentrated in software and staples, with Salesforce down 3.94% and Netflix down 3.28% the worst of the group.
note.rates:
The curve steepened with yields falling across the board, a bear steepener in the sense that the move was led by front-end declines rather than long-end selling. 2s10s widened 6bp to 38bp and 5s30s widened 7bp to 66bp, while 3m10y narrowed 2bp to 67bp. The 2-year fell 12bp to 4.46%, the 5-year fell 10bp to 4.59%, the 10-year fell 6bp to 4.84%, and the 30-year fell 3bp to 5.25%.

Breakevens were mixed and small. The 5-year breakeven rose 3bp to 2.29% while the 10-year breakeven fell 1bp to 2.23%, and the 5y5y forward fell 5bp to 2.17%. Real yields, via the 10-year TIPS, fell 4bp to 2.60%. The MOVE index fell 5.26% to 92.77, consistent with the broad decline in rate volatility seen in the risk barometer detail.
note.credit: Credit did not confirm the equity or rates move. LQD fell 0.12% and HYG fell 0.07%, with high yield as tracked by JNK down 0.09% and sitting among the session's lows. EM sovereign debt via EMB was flat on the day. Leveraged loans, by contrast, rose 0.25% on BKLN. The tone is cautious rather than constructive: credit spreads widened modestly while equities and rate vol both improved, a combination that argues for watching credit as the tiebreaker.
note.fx: The dollar index rose 0.72% to 102.28 and sits among the session's highs, a firm move against a broad complex. EUR/USD fell 0.82% to 1.114 and GBP/USD fell 0.90% to 1.336, both weak. AUD/USD was the laggard in G10, down 1.94% to 0.687. USD/JPY was little changed, up 0.04% to 158.43. In EM, USD/TRY rose 0.19% to 50.134 and sits at a session high, USD/BRL rose 0.68%, while USD/CNY fell 0.12% to 6.665 and USD/MXN fell 0.06%, both at or near session lows for the pair.
note.commodities: Crude held a narrow range, WTI down 0.20% to $90.34 and Brent down 0.54% to $97.76. Natural gas rose 1.90%. Precious metals softened despite the weaker-dollar-adjacent rate backdrop: gold fell 0.83% to $4,079.50 and silver fell 0.51%, while platinum rose 0.83% and palladium fell 1.87%. Copper rose 0.18% to $6.26, holding its year-to-date gain. Grains and softs were mixed: wheat fell 1.46%, corn rose 0.51%, soybeans rose 1.14%, coffee rose 1.08%, cocoa rose 1.12%, and sugar fell 1.67%.
note.volatility: The vol complex eased broadly. VIX fell 9.01% to 25.64 and VIX9D fell 16.78% to 27.18, a sharper drop at the front end than in VIX3M, down 3.72% to 24.60, which flattens the term structure from an inverted starting point. VVIX fell 9.67% to 121.94, suggesting the drop in implied vol was not purely mechanical. SKEW rose 2.80% to 153.55, so tail protection got modestly more expensive even as at-the-money vol came in. The MOVE index fell 5.26%, in step with the equity vol decline.
note.digital: Bitcoin was flat on the day, down 0.01% to $75,937.56, showing little beta to the equity move despite the Nasdaq's 1.35% gain. Ether rose 0.17% and Solana rose 1.23%, modest gains that track risk sentiment loosely. XRP fell 2.21%, the weakest of the group. The complex is not confirming the equity rally with any conviction.
note.international: European markets closed lower across the board ahead of the US session, with the DAX down 1.92%, EURO STOXX 50 down 0.98%, and the FTSE 100 down 1.01%. Asia was broadly weaker too: the Nikkei fell 5.97%, KOSPI fell 6.02%, and TAIEX fell 4.51%, a sharp regional selloff that New York did not inherit. The Sensex was the outlier, up 2.17%. The handoff to the US session was a risk-off tone in Asia and Europe that the afternoon's tech-led US bid pushed against rather than confirmed.
note.correlation:
The session broke the recent pattern of equities and rates moving together on a single growth or policy narrative. Yields fell across the curve while equities rose, and the dollar rose at the same time, a combination that is hard to explain with one factor. Credit spreads widened modestly while equity vol compressed, another split that argues more than one force was in play, possibly single-name earnings reactions in mega-cap tech sitting on top of a separate rates and dollar move.

A break worth watching is whether gold keeps falling alongside lower real yields. Gold fell 0.83% while the 10-year TIPS yield fell 4bp, a pairing that normally moves together. If that divergence persists, it points to dollar strength or a liquidity need dominating the gold price rather than the usual real-yield driver, and would argue against reading today's cross-asset moves through a single growth lens.
